Hi Julia / Aaron —

Thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we spin up the POC environment.

Recap (from our conversation)
- Goal: Validate latency and cost profile for the customer-facing chat assistant and the reranking pipeline for search.
- Primary success criteria: 95th percentile latency < 350ms for 512-token responses under steady-state RPS; end-to-end cost per 1k prompts within target range (you provided a target range during the demo).

What we need from you to finalize the POC scope (traffic intake)
1) Steady-state RPS and peak/burst RPS (per region).
2) Typical and max input/output token lengths (avg, p95, max).
3) Concurrency expectations (number of parallel users/sessions).
4) Any prepended system prompts or long-context usage (e.g., KV cache sizes).
5) Any regulatory constraints on data residency (you mentioned EU).

I attached a traffic sample stub (finteq-traffic-sample.json) — please replace with an anonymized export or confirm the numbers in your reply.

Proposed evaluation plan / timeline
- Feb 22: Provision staging environment + API keys; Redwood SE (Karthik) and your infra contact verify connectivity.
- Feb 23–24: Throughput & latency runs (steady-state and synthetic bursts).
- Feb 25: Quality checks vs. your eval prompts and cost/latency analysis.
- Feb 26: Joint review; decision on next steps (scale to Dedicated/Private or iterate).

Ownership
- Redwood: Marissa (engagement lead), Karthik (solutions engineer — throughput/benchmark runs), Dev (integration harness).
- Finteq: Julia (PM owner), Aaron (infra / network).

Success criteria (draft — please confirm):
- Latency: p95 generation time < 350ms at steady-state RPS for responses <= 512 tokens.
- Throughput: handle steady-state RPS with <2% error rate and recover from 5x bursts within 30s.
- Cost: token cost per 1k prompts within the range you outlined (you said ~€X–€Y).
- Functional: model accuracy/quality delta relative to your baseline within acceptable tolerance (you'll provide prompt set).

Next steps for you: please reply with the traffic numbers requested above and attach an anonymized log if possible. If Feb 22–26 works we’ll reserve slots on our Dedicated staging cluster.

Thanks — looking forward.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear note. Below are the traffic numbers based on last month’s anonymized logs (attached as finteq-anon-logs.csv). Let me know if you need a different granularity.

Traffic summary
- Steady-state RPS: 120 RPS (EU panel)
- Typical daytime concurrency: ~30 concurrent sessions; peak concurrency during campaigns ~140
- Burst patterns: daily small spikes (~1.5–2x lasting <2m), marketing sends produce bursts up to 3.5–4x that can last 5–10m; observed one event last month hitting ~450 RPS for ~8 minutes.
- Token lengths:
  • Avg request tokens (user prompt): 75 tokens
  • Avg response tokens: 120 tokens
  • p95 request tokens: 240
  • max observed response tokens: 1,200 (rare)
- Usage mix: ~70% one-shot prompt; ~25% 2–3 turn sessions (light context reuse); ~5% long context workflows (knowledge retrieval + synthesis).

Constraints
- Data residency: all EU customer PII must remain in EU region.
- IAM: Aaron (copied) will handle network-level access.

We confirm we can do Feb 22–26 for the POC window. Aaron will coordinate on connectivity and ephemeral keys.

Key adjustments and ask for sign-off
- Staging sizing: we’ll target a cluster capable of 600 RPS sustained to cover steady-state + headroom for bursts (this maps to our 4-GPU Dedicated staging config).
- Token budget and warmup: because you have occasional 1,200-token responses, we’ll run a p95/p99 workload including the long-tail sample to validate memory/KV cache behavior.
- Test harness: Dev will provide a small JMeter/Locust harness (scripted to reproduce your burst patterns).
- Throughput runs: Karthik will schedule steady-state runs at 120 RPS and burst tests up to 500 RPS to measure recovery and queueing.

Draft success criteria (finalized once you supply a small eval prompt set):
1) p95 generation latency < 350ms for responses <=512 tokens at 120 RPS steady-state.
2) System recovers from 450 RPS burst to steady-state in <30s with <2% error rate.
3) End-to-end token cost estimate within target band (we will provide a cost model during the POC).
4) No EU data leaves region; logs stored per GDPR requirements (we will provide audit config).

Action items (owners):
- Finteq: provide the eval prompt set (Julia) + infra contact for key exchange (Aaron).
- Redwood: provide ephemeral API key + test harness (Dev), schedule runs and analysis (Karthik), MOP and report (Marissa).

If you confirm we’ll: (a) reserve the staging cluster on Feb 21 for validation, (b) send ephemeral keys and the harness, (c) schedule the first run for Feb 23.

Thanks — can you confirm the eval prompt set by EOD Wednesday?

Marissa / Dev — quick technical notes ahead of the runs.

On Thu, Feb 12, 2026 11:45 AM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Perfect — thanks for the numbers, Julia. I’ve updated the POC plan in the shared Drive link...

Notes:
- Batching strategy: for 120 RPS with avg request tokens ~75 and avg response ~120, continuous batching (200–300ms batch window) should reduce token cost and keep latency within targets. For burst runs we’ll shorten the batch window to 50ms but increase parallel workers to maintain throughput.
- KV cache warm-up: long-context sessions (1,200 tokens) will require warm-up sequences to populate KV caches. Schedule a warm-up phase (~5–10 minutes) before each burst test.
- Concurrency: target harness concurrency of 30 for steady-state; run a separate test for high concurrency (140 concurrent sessions) to validate connection and session handling.
- Model variants: we should test a quantized 4-bit variant for cost baseline, then a higher-precision runtime for quality check.
- Metrics to collect: p50/p95/p99 latency (generation + round-trip), GPU utilization, mem high-water marks, queue depth, error codes, token counts per request.

Requests for Finteq (Aaron) before Feb 22:
1) Confirm EU VPC peering window and whether we should use a private endpoint.
2) Provide a small set (50–100) of eval prompts and 10 long-tail examples for p99 behavior.
3) Confirm whether synthetic users should authenticate as real users or as anonymous test clients (affects session affinity).

I’ll prepare the Locust scripts and a short runbook for interpreting the output.

— Karthik
